result_text: {"verdict":"ACCEPT_SCOPED","exact_accepted_claim":"Theorems 1 and 2 are accepted exactly as scoped in the bound proof.md (SHA256 1f225321…), and nothing broader. Common hypotheses: any finite conflict graph G on n ≥ 1 links, with independent-set family I(G). Arrival vectors A(t) are iid over slots, with 0 ≤ A_i(t) ≤ a_* < ∞ and mean λ, added at slot end. Q(0) is deterministic and finite, and work is divisible. The channel process, the arrival sequence and all clock/mark randomness are mutually independent. Strict admissibility holds in the proof's additive sense: λ+ε1 ≤ r(α) = Σ_c π(c)Σ_σ α_c(σ)(c_iσ_i)_i for some ε > 0 and channel-indexed distributions α_c on I(G). Carrier sensing is perfect, instantaneous and edge-exact, with no collisions, hidden terminals or propagation delay. There is a common epoch, synchronized slot boundaries and a shared slot counter. Access probabilities are exact real numbers, and each link observes its own channel exactly and instantaneously. Theorem 1: C(t) is a finite-state irreducible (possibly periodic) discrete-time Markov chain in [0,c_*]^n with arbitrary initial law, constant within each slot. Controller (1)–(2) resets bits to 0 and runs heat-bath updates with p_i = e^{Q_i(t)C_i(t)}/(1+e^{Q_i(t)C_i(t)}) on independent Poisson clocks of rate R_t = exp((t+1)²) over the paid window [t,t+δ_t), with δ_t = 1/(t+2). It then serves (1−δ_t)C_i(t)σ_i(t). Theorem 2: C(u), u ≥ 0, is a finite-state irreducible continuous-time Markov jump chain in [0,c_*]^n. It has generator Γ, stationary law π, arbitrary initial law, and finite γ_* = max_c(−Γ_cc), which the policy does not know. At each integer t the controller resets bits to 0 and holds q_i = Q_i(t). It runs rate-R_t clocks on all of [t,t+1), with heat-bath probability p_i(u) = e^{q_iC_i(u)}/(1+e^{q_iC_i(u)}) computed from the link's own current channel. Data is withheld on [t,t+δ_t). Afterwards a link with bit 1 serves at its current rate C_i(u), with zero-time switching and no minimum packet duration, and empty links keep dummy reservation activity. Service and queue update are (C1). Conclusion of each theorem: for some θ > 0, sup_{t∈Z+} E exp(θ‖Q(t)‖_2) < ∞. The constants depend on the model primitives and Q(0) (and, for Theorem 2, on γ_* through K^ct) but not on t. Hence sup_t E Σ_i Q_i(t) < ∞ and the printed condition (B2) holds. For Theorem 2 the bound also holds at all real times, since queues do not increase within a slot. Also accepted, each only in its stated role. §5.1 (unique stationary law (13,37,29)/158 per channel state; useful service 37/79 versus frozen-Gibbs 9/11) is accepted as a falsification of the instantaneous-product-form shortcut at comparable clock and channel rates, not as an impossibility result. §5.2 is accepted as an architecture-specific capacity loss for a fixed control fraction. §5.3 (average backlog (2K+7)/12 → ∞ with bounded deterministic arrivals of mean 1/2, while Q(t)/t → 0) is accepted as proof that the book's mean-rate-only arrival hypothesis is insufficient for (B2). Not accepted: any resolution of the book's problem; any simple, low-cost, bounded-rate, time-homogeneous, counter-free or physically implementable scheduler; channels with continuously varying capacities, or non-Markov, infinite-state or unbounded-rate channels; delayed or imperfect CSI or sensing; positive switching or guard times; non-iid or unbounded arrivals; any novelty or literature-positioning claim; any checker output.","findings":[{"id":"R1-AUDIT","severity":"info (prior findings re-checked; no regression)","location":"evidence/claude-review.json F1–F10 and V0 versus current proof.md §2, Lemmas 1–5, §4, §5.1","issue":"The round-1 receipt binds proof.md ba43e930…, not the bound 1f225321…. Per referee-dispositions.json it covered Theorem 1 only, so it is not acceptance of the current text or of Theorem 2. Each item was re-checked against the current text. F1 is fixed: r(α) is defined before strict admissibility. F2 is fixed: F_t is generated by Q(0), C(0..t), A(0..t−1) and the clocks/marks of earlier slots, and the text states mutual independence of the three primitive families, an arbitrary initial channel law, and E[f(C(t+k))|F_t] = (P^k f)(C(t)). F3 is fixed: TV is the sup over events, i.e. half the L1 distance. F4 is fixed ('finite but superexponentially growing local rates', 'finite constant'). Declining the optional polynomial-K remark is acceptable, since nothing depends on it. F5 is adopted in substance: the counter is named as a surrogate for a global queue-growth bound, and the sampler cost is exposed. Declining round 1's 'intrinsic superexponential cost' assertion is justified. Under standard complexity assumptions, its Markov-inequality reduction at most rules out cost polynomial in n and in the log of the weight scale on all graphs. The superexponential dependence on t comes from not knowing q_*, a_*, c_* and n. F6 is fixed. F7 still applies (see PROV). F8 is fixed (irreducibility plus swap invariance). F9 needs no change. F10 is fixed (the three desiderata are separated). An independent analytic re-derivation of Lemmas 1–5 on the current text found no regression. Detailed balance holds for (5). The marked coupling has the controller's law. Each window of length 1/R_t sends every copy to the all-zero state with probability e^{−n}∏(1−p_i). 1+e^w ≤ 2e^w gives (8). The entropy identity gives a loss of at most log|I(G)| ≤ n log2. (1−δ_t)E W ≥ E W − δ_tH_t gives (9). (10)–(11) are finite, with H_tδ_t ≤ n c_* max(q_*/2, a_*). (13) is solvable for periodic P. Theorem 1 stands as previously assessed. Channel variation enters only across slots. The per-slot reset and a clock with R_tδ_t ≫ (2e)^n e^{H_t} make each slot an essentially exact Gibbs sample for the current (Q,C). The analysis therefore reduces to MaxWeight with additive error under Markov modulation. Theorem 2 genuinely removes per-slot freezing: jumps may occur at any real time during control or data, service follows the current channel, and the chain re-adapts through own-channel observation at rings. Its tracking, however, comes from time-scale separation constructed in two directions. The clock outruns the e^{O(t)} queue-weight mixing scale, and the vanishing window makes any fixed channel speed asymptotically slow; the resulting error H_tγ_*δ_t is bounded but linear in γ_*. The printed difficulty is the feedback between adaptive access, queues and time-varying rates without such separation, which is the §5.1 regime. That difficulty is bypassed, not reduced. Additions beyond the supplied printed text: (1) iid bounded arrivals; §5.3 rightly shows some regularity is needed. (2) Finite-state irreducible Markov channels, either slotted or piecewise-constant continuous-time, with bounded exit rate. (3) Exact instantaneous own-channel CSI, made continuous with zero-delay rate adaptation in Theorem 2. (4) Perfect, instantaneous, edge-exact sensing with no collisions, hidden terminals or propagation delay. (5) Zero-time data/reservation switching and no minimum packet duration (Theorem 2). (6) A common epoch, synchronized slot boundaries and a synchronized data start. (7) Real-valued access probabilities. (8) Divisible work, with dummy activity by empty links. (9) Deterministic Q(0). (10) Expected rings per slot of n e^{(t+1)²}/(t+2) for Theorem 1 and n e^{(t+1)²} for Theorem 2. Against the printed desiderata: 'simple' fails, because control work is superexponential in t. 'Distributed' holds only given global synchronization and the shared counter. 'Memoryless' holds statewise at slot boundaries for Theorem 1 and with one held local queue sample per slot for Theorem 2, but both controllers are time-inhomogeneous through the counter. The oracle audit passes: no runtime global maximum, graph size or model parameter is used. The caveats are adequate in substance: the PARTIAL label, explicit costs and idealizations, and no efficiency or novelty claim. They become fully adequate after the S1–S5 wording fixes. These cover 'continuously changing', the undefined 'autonomous', the engineered channel time-scale separation and γ_*-linear constant, the 'avoidable proof gap' phrasing, and continuous-CSI rate adaptation.","novelty_assessment":"No novelty is claimed and none was found. Theorem 1 combines standard ingredients: the CSMA/Glauber product form for the weighted hard-core model; a Doeblin all-zero coalescence bound; the Gibbs variational inequality, with loss at most log|I(G)|; a T-slot quadratic drift with a Poisson-equation correction for Markov-modulated service; and a Hajek-type conversion to a uniform exponential moment. Theorem 2 adds a standard perturbation step: a no-jump window with probability ≥ 1−γ_*δ_t, uniform-in-initial-state mixing on that window, and the continuous-time Poisson equation via Dynkin. This is a clean, modest extension that is routine once the counter-driven clock is granted. The single design device, a superexponential counter-indexed clock with a vanishing paid window, is time-scale separation by construction. It contributes no technique that transfers to bounded-rate, time-homogeneous, counter-free controllers. Positioning is unverified because no primary source is supplied. This applies to Yun–Shin–Yi 2013/2016, which per status.json give rate stability with Q_max-dependent log-log weights; to Li–Eryilmaz, Swamy–Ganti–Jagannathan and Shneer–Stolyar; and to background-recalled work such as Jiang–Walrand, Rajagopalan–Shah–Shin, Shah–Shin and Ni–Tan–Srikant. status.json is a secondary summary, and per supplement-access.json the YSY2016 supplementary proofs remain unread. F1 is fixed: r(α) is defined before strict admissibility. F2 is fixed: F_t is generated by Q(0), C(0..t), A(0..t−1) and the clocks/marks of earlier slots, and the text states mutual independence of the three primitive families, an arbitrary initial channel law, and E[f(C(t+k))|F_t] = (P^k f)(C(t)). F3 is fixed: TV is the sup over events, i.e. half the L1 distance. F4 is fixed ('finite but superexponentially growing local rates', 'finite constant'). Declining the optional polynomial-K remark is acceptable, since nothing depends on it. F5 is adopted in substance: the counter is named as a surrogate for a global queue-growth bound, and the sampler cost is exposed. Declining round 1's 'intrinsic superexponential cost' assertion is justified. Under standard complexity assumptions, its Markov-inequality reduction at most rules out cost polynomial in n and in the log of the weight scale on all graphs. The superexponential dependence on t comes from not knowing q_*, a_*, c_* and n. F6 is fixed. F7 still applies (see PROV). F8 is fixed (irreducibility plus swap invariance). F9 needs no change. F10 is fixed (the three desiderata are separated). An independent analytic re-derivation of Lemmas 1–5 on the current text found no regression. Detailed balance holds for (5). The marked coupling has the controller's law. Each window of length 1/R_t sends every copy to the all-zero state with probability e^{−n}∏(1−p_i). 1+e^w ≤ 2e^w gives (8). The entropy identity gives a loss of at most log|I(G)| ≤ n log2. (1−δ_t)E W ≥ E W − δ_tH_t gives (9). (10)–(11) are finite, with H_tδ_t ≤ n c_* max(q_*/2, a_*). (13) is solvable for periodic P. The replacement error is Σ_k nD²k = nD²T(T−1)/2. (16)–(19) hold with ρ ∈ [3/4,1).

findings.location: §3A: (C1)–(C7), K^ct, reuse of Lemma 5, continuous-time conclusion
findings.issue: Every bridge of the extension was re-derived analytically; no code was run. (C2): u ≥ t+δ_t gives u−δ_t ≥ t. The jump compensator satisfies ∫γ(C(s))ds ≤ γ_*δ_t. Mutual independence makes C Markov with respect to the enlarged F_t, which contains the channel path on [0,t]. Window step: E_u and C(u) are path-measurable, and on E_u the weights q_iC_i(s) are constant on (u−δ_t,u]. σ(u−δ_t) is a function of the path and of the slot-t clock/mark increments on [t,u−δ_t]. The window increments are independent of all of these and of F_t, so the frozen chain runs for duration δ_t at rate R_t. Lemma 2 is uniform in the initial state, and Σ_iq_iC_i(u) ≤ H_t still holds because Q_i(t) ≤ q_*+a_*t is unchanged. Together these give TV ≤ η_t, and convexity of TV handles the mixture over σ(u−δ_t). (C3): E[W·1_{E_u}|F_t] ≥ E[1_{E_u}(W_max−n log2−H_tη_t)|F_t] and E[1_{E_u^c}W_max|F_t] ≤ H_tγ_*δ_t together give (C3) exactly. Jumps during control are covered because the window may straddle t+δ_t. (C4)/(C5): integrating over [t+δ_t,t+1] with 1−δ_t ≤ 1 and ∫_t^{t+δ_t}W_max ≤ H_tδ_t gives K^ct = n log2 + sup_t H_t{η_t+(1+γ_*)δ_t} < ∞. Fubini is valid for bounded càdlàg integrands. Dummy activity keeps the bit process equal to the frozen-q heat-bath chain after a queue empties. With no mid-slot arrivals, the actual service is min(Q_i(t),S_i(t)), consistent with (C1). (C6): ker Γ = constants by the maximum principle, the left kernel is span π, and the range is {v: πv = 0}. (C7): Dynkin gives E∫_t^{t+T}s_i du = Tr_i + h_i(C(t)) − E h_i(C(t+T)). Drift: S_i ≤ (1−δ_t)c_*, so B is unchanged. In the one-slot bound, |λ_i − E[∫s_i|F_{t+k}]| ≤ D and the tower property give the nD²T(T−1)/2 replacement error. T ≥ 4max_i‖h_i‖_∞/ε then gives (12). Lemma 5 needs only (12) and per-slot increments in [−c_*,a_*]. Queues are nonincreasing within a slot. Theorem 2 is therefore proved under its stated hypotheses.

findings.location: §3A window argument: 'Future link-clock increments and their independent marks are independent of that path'
findings.issue: Applying Lemma 2 uniformly over the initial state requires the clock points and marks on (u−δ_t,u] to be independent of the triple (F_t, entire channel path, σ(u−δ_t)), not merely of the path. This holds: slot-t clocks are independent marked Poisson processes with independent increments, σ(u−δ_t) is a function of the path and of earlier increments, and the three primitive families are mutually independent. The text does not say this. It also leaves implicit that 'its own current channel' at a ring is a.s. unambiguous, because clock rings and channel jumps a.s. never coincide.
findings.required_fix: Construct slot-t control randomness explicitly as independent rate-R_t marked Poisson processes with iid uniform marks, independent of the channel path, the arrivals and earlier slots. State the conditional independence of the window increments from (F_t, path, σ(u−δ_t)). Note a.s. non-coincidence of rings and jumps.

findings.issue: (C4) writes E∫_t^{t+1}W_max(q,C(u))du without '|F_t', although q = Q(t) is random and the inequality is conditional. (C7) is likewise conditional on C(t), or equivalently on F_t, as the following sentence acknowledges. This is a notation issue only.
findings.required_fix: Write E[∫_t^{t+1}W_max(Q(t),C(u))du | F_t] in (C4) and E[·|F_t] in (C7).

findings.location: §1 ('continuously changing finite-state Markov channels'); framing of Theorem 2
findings.issue: The Theorem 2 channel is a finite-state CTMC: its paths are piecewise constant with total jump intensity at most γ_*. The proof uses exactly this, through P(E_u^c) ≤ γ_*δ_t. It does not cover capacities that vary continuously in time (continuous fading models, where a no-change window has probability 0), non-Markov or infinite-state channels, or unbounded jump rates. 'Continuously changing' suggests more than is proved. The §3A heading 'Continuous-time Markov channels' is accurate.
findings.required_fix: Replace 'continuously changing' with 'finite-state continuous-time Markov jump channels whose state may change at any real time, with finite maximal exit rate'. List continuously varying capacities among the excluded models.

findings.location: §3A ('The unknown channel speed enters the proof constant, not the policy'; 'fast but finite channel dynamics create only a uniform additive … error'); §4 ('surrogate for a global queue-growth bound'); Lemma 2 heading
findings.issue: In Theorem 2 the counter also substitutes for knowledge of channel speed. δ_t → 0 while γ_* is fixed, so every fixed channel becomes asymptotically quasi-static relative to the paid window, while R_tδ_t ≫ (2e)^n e^{H_t} keeps the heat-bath chain mixed inside that window. Tracking is therefore obtained by time-scale separation constructed in two directions: control against queue-weight growth, and control against channel dynamics. Asymptotically the controller leaves the §5.1 regime of comparable clock and channel rates, where product form fails and service drops from 9/11 to 37/79. Theorem 2 therefore says nothing about controllers whose rates are comparable to the channel dynamics, which is where the printed interaction difficulty lives. The channel term in K^ct, sup_t H_tγ_*δ_t ≤ γ_* n c_* max(q_*/2,a_*), is linear in γ_*. It propagates through K_T, r_0, b and M into (19), so the error is uniform in time but grows with channel speed. Lemma 2's heading ('without a time-scale separation assumption') is true only in the sense that the separation is built by the clock schedule rather than assumed.
findings.required_fix: In §3A and §4, state that the counter substitutes for unknown queue-growth bounds and unknown channel-speed bounds, and that Theorem 2 rests on constructed separation between control and channel time scales. State that the additive error is uniform in t but linear in γ_*. Qualify Lemma 2's heading accordingly.

findings.location: §4 final paragraph ('For an autonomous local-queue/local-channel A-CSMA controller in continuously changing finite-state Markov channels, what is still missing here is …')
findings.issue: 'Autonomous' is never defined. Theorem 2's controller is a local-queue/local-channel random-access controller in finite-state Markov channels, and it does achieve a (20)-type drift, namely (12). The paragraph's demand for 'an actual control/channel tracking bound with additive weighted-service error, uniform in the initial schedule' is exactly what (C3)–(C5) supply for that controller. The paragraph appears to predate Theorem 2. It is consistent only if 'autonomous' means time-homogeneous, counter-free, and bounded-rate or state-dependent-rate.
findings.required_fix: Define 'autonomous' in that sense. State that Theorem 2 supplies (20) only for the counter-driven, unbounded-rate controller.

findings.location: §4 first paragraph ('separates a genuine issue (the attainable control speed and information architecture) from an avoidable proof gap'; 'closes … every bridge')
findings.issue: Nothing is proved about bounded-rate or counter-free controllers, so the text cannot assert that the residual difficulty is merely architectural rather than mathematical. As written, it suggests the book's open problem has been reduced to engineering.
findings.required_fix: Rephrase: given unbounded, synchronized, counter-driven control speed, no further mathematical obstruction remains for this proof template; nothing is established for bounded-rate, time-homogeneous local controllers.

findings.issue: The list covers sensing, propagation, switching time and guard times. It omits that serving at the 'current channel rate' requires exact, zero-delay, continuous own-channel tracking and rate adaptation at every channel jump, including jumps between clock rings, not only observation at rings. The book's listed future directions single out delayed or inaccurate CSI.
findings.required_fix: Add continuous exact own-channel CSI with instantaneous rate adaptation to the Theorem 2 assumption list.

findings.issue: Re-derived by hand. The out-rates are 12/5, 11/10 and 3/2, and a channel flip maps good-active to bad-active across states. All four displayed equations follow, with unique solution (13,37,29)/158. Service is 2·37/158 = 37/79, versus 9/(1+9+1) = 9/11. With clock rate R and the same channel, the balance equations are −14a+b+5d = 0, 0.9Ra−(0.1R+1)b+d = 0 and 0.5Ra+b−(0.5R+1)d = 0. At R = 100 they give (7,58,8)/146, matching the check.json entry. As R→∞ they give (1,9,1)/22, so service → 9/11. The example therefore refutes the shortcut only at comparable time scales, and Theorem 2 escapes it solely through R_t → ∞, which reinforces S2.
findings.required_fix: Optional: state the R→∞ limit to connect §5.1 with Theorem 2's mechanism.

findings.issue: §5.2: service of at most 3/4 per slot against arrivals of 7/8 gives backlog ≥ Q(0)+t/8. §5.3: the cycle-k pre-slot values are 0,2,3,…,k and then k+1,k,…,1,0,…, and the queue empties because 3k ≥ k+1. The per-cycle sum is (k(k+1)/2−1)+(k+1)(k+2)/2 = k²+2k. The time through cycle K is 2K(K+1), so the average is [K(K+1)(2K+7)/6]/[2K(K+1)] = (2K+7)/12. The maximum k+1 is O(√t), and the arrival mean is 1/2 along all t. A single work-conserving server is pathwise queue-minimal, so no policy at all satisfies (B2) on this input. The roles assigned to these examples (architecture limit; assumption gap only) are stated accurately.
findings.required_fix: None. Optionally state the any-policy strengthening.

findings.issue: Runtime inputs are the link's own Q_i(t); its own channel (at slot start for Theorem 1, continuously for Theorem 2); neighbours' reservation bits via sensing; the slot counter t, for R_t and δ_t; and synchronized slot boundaries and data start. No Q_max, n, a_*, c_*, γ_*, λ, P/Γ, π, α, h, H_t, K or K^ct is used at runtime, and no MaxWeight output is consumed. The shared counter is global timing information acting as a surrogate for global bounds. This is disclosed for queue growth but not for channel speed (S2).

review.scope_assessment: Both theorems are valid but deliberately impractical scoped results, not a solution of the book problem, and PARTIAL is the correct book-level label. Theorem 1 stands as previously assessed. Channel variation enters only across slots. The per-slot reset and a clock with R_tδ_t ≫ (2e)^n e^{H_t} make each slot an essentially exact Gibbs sample for the current (Q,C). The analysis therefore reduces to MaxWeight with additive error under Markov modulation. Theorem 2 genuinely removes per-slot freezing: jumps may occur at any real time during control or data, service follows the current channel, and the chain re-adapts through own-channel observation at rings. Its tracking, however, comes from time-scale separation constructed in two directions. The clock outruns the e^{O(t)} queue-weight mixing scale, and the vanishing window makes any fixed channel speed asymptotically slow; the resulting error H_tγ_*δ_t is bounded but linear in γ_*. The printed difficulty is the feedback between adaptive access, queues and time-varying rates without such separation, which is the §5.1 regime. That difficulty is bypassed, not reduced. Additions beyond the supplied printed text: (1) iid bounded arrivals; §5.3 rightly shows some regularity is needed. (2) Finite-state irreducible Markov channels, either slotted or piecewise-constant continuous-time, with bounded exit rate. (3) Exact instantaneous own-channel CSI, made continuous with zero-delay rate adaptation in Theorem 2. (4) Perfect, instantaneous, edge-exact sensing with no collisions, hidden terminals or propagation delay. (5) Zero-time data/reservation switching and no minimum packet duration (Theorem 2). (6) A common epoch, synchronized slot boundaries and a synchronized data start. (7) Real-valued access probabilities. (8) Divisible work, with dummy activity by empty links. (9) Deterministic Q(0). (10) Expected rings per slot of n e^{(t+1)²}/(t+2) for Theorem 1 and n e^{(t+1)²} for Theorem 2. Against the printed desiderata: 'simple' fails, because control work is superexponential in t. 'Distributed' holds only given global synchronization and the shared counter. 'Memoryless' holds statewise at slot boundaries for Theorem 1 and with one held local queue sample per slot for Theorem 2, but both controllers are time-inhomogeneous through the counter. The oracle audit passes: no runtime global maximum, graph size or model parameter is used. The caveats are adequate in substance: the PARTIAL label, explicit costs and idealizations, and no efficiency or novelty claim. They become fully adequate after the S1–S5 wording fixes. These cover 'continuously changing', the undefined 'autonomous', the engineered channel time-scale separation and γ_*-linear constant, the 'avoidable proof gap' phrasing, and continuous-CSI rate adaptation.
review.novelty_assessment: No novelty is claimed and none was found. Theorem 1 combines standard ingredients: the CSMA/Glauber product form for the weighted hard-core model; a Doeblin all-zero coalescence bound; the Gibbs variational inequality, with loss at most log|I(G)|; a T-slot quadratic drift with a Poisson-equation correction for Markov-modulated service; and a Hajek-type conversion to a uniform exponential moment. Theorem 2 adds a standard perturbation step: a no-jump window with probability ≥ 1−γ_*δ_t, uniform-in-initial-state mixing on that window, and the continuous-time Poisson equation via Dynkin. This is a clean, modest extension that is routine once the counter-driven clock is granted. The single design device, a superexponential counter-indexed clock with a vanishing paid window, is time-scale separation by construction. It contributes no technique that transfers to bounded-rate, time-homogeneous, counter-free controllers. Positioning is unverified because no primary source is supplied. This applies to Yun–Shin–Yi 2013/2016, which per status.json give rate stability with Q_max-dependent log-log weights; to Li–Eryilmaz, Swamy–Ganti–Jagannathan and Shneer–Stolyar; and to background-recalled work such as Jiang–Walrand, Rajagopalan–Shah–Shin, Shah–Shin and Ni–Tan–Srikant. status.json is a secondary summary, and per supplement-access.json the YSY2016 supplementary proofs remain unread. Whether a counter-driven strong-stability statement of this kind already exists is unknown, so 'NOVELTY-UNCLEAR' is the appropriate label.
review.first_independent_check: Without reusing work/check.py, test the only new probabilistic bridge, (C2)–(C4), exactly on the smallest nontrivial instance. Take one conflict edge (n = 2) and a two-state channel CTMC with rate γ, for example the §5.1 capacity states (1,0)/(0,1) or capacities (1/2,1/2)/(1,1). Fix q and set H = Σ_i q_i c_*. Build the 6-state joint channel×schedule generator for one slot: heat-bath addition rates R·p_i(c), removal rates R·(1−p_i(c)), plus the channel rates. Starting from schedule 0 and each channel state, compute the exact law at times u ∈ [δ,1] by rational or interval-arithmetic matrix exponential. Use a grid of (R,δ,γ) that includes γ comparable to R (the §5.1 regime) and Rδ ≫ (2e)²e^H. For every u, check E[q·C(u)σ(u)] ≥ E[W_max(q,C(u))] − 2log2 − H(exp(−(2e)^{−2}e^{−H}⌊Rδ⌋) + γδ). The proof establishes this for arbitrary R and δ, so a violation at any parameters would refute it. Then check the integrated form (C4). Also check that, conditioned on no jump in (u−δ,u], the schedule law is within (1−p(w))^{⌊Rδ⌋} of ν_{q,C(u)} from every starting schedule. In the same pass, solve the §5.1 6×6 generator without the symmetry ansatz at R = 1 and R = 100. Expect (13,37,29)/158 and (7,58,8)/146 per channel state, and confirm the R→∞ limit (1,9,1)/22, which gives service 9/11. Finally, write out the product probability space (channel path × arrival sequence × independent marked Poisson clocks per link and slot). Confirm that one filtration F_t simultaneously yields (7)/(C3), E[A(t)|F_t] = λ, and the Markov identities used in (14)/(C7).
